faq_items.question: What size should living room wall art be above the sofa?
faq_items.answer: Living room wall art should span about two-thirds to three-quarters of your sofa's width, with its center around 57-60 inches from the floor. For a standard 84-inch sofa, aim for art or a grouping roughly 55-63 inches wide, leaving 6-8 inches above the sofa back.

faq_items.question: How do I print wall art at home so it looks professional?
faq_items.answer: Use heavyweight matte cardstock instead of copy paper, set your printer to its highest quality, and choose Actual Size or 100% scale rather than Fit to Page. For prints larger than letter size, take the file to a local print shop for sharper, more color-accurate results.

faq_items.question: Is this living room wall art really free to download?
faq_items.answer: Yes. Every design is a free, high-resolution printable with no watermark and no purchase required. You only pay for your own paper, ink, and frames, and you can reprint the set anytime your color scheme or room changes.

faq_items.question: What style of wall art works best in a living room?
faq_items.answer: Warm-neutral abstract and mid-century styles work best because they complement rather than compete with your furniture. Terracotta, sage, ochre, cream, and soft black read as calm and curated, and abstract designs have no literal subject to clash with your existing decor.

faq_items.question: How do I frame printable wall art cheaply?
faq_items.answer: Design prints to standard sizes (8x10, 11x14, 16x20) so they fit ready-made frames from any craft or big-box store, usually under $15 each. Use a matching set of simple frames for a cohesive look and removable adhesive strips to hang them without nails.
